reviewed_declarations.name: AuditRound12.audit_root

reviewed_declarations.name: AuditRound12.basis_relations
reviewed_declarations.reason: All n: PBe=Be, PBo=-Bo, both Gram matrices 2I, mixed Gram zero, SBe=BoE, SBo=BeE. Direct block multiplication verifies all seven conjuncts. Empty matrices satisfy the same statements; for n>0 the Gram matrices guarantee column independence.

reviewed_declarations.name: AuditRound12.convention_bridge
reviewed_declarations.reason: Implicit n and arbitrary K. Replacing both S/E by their negatives preserves conjugation and the column relations. The two normalized exchange formulas follow by common scaling 1/2. This is an optional convention conversion: the intended one-based (-1)^(j+1) already agrees with zero-based (-1)^i.

reviewed_declarations.name: AuditRound12.coordinate_bridge
reviewed_declarations.reason: All n, with the Fin n and Pair n binders intact: both coordinate positions, swap/reversal, sign parity and P/S pullbacks. For a right-half index, i<n implies n>=1, so 2n-1-i has opposite parity to i; no subtraction problem survives at n=0 because those index quantifiers are empty.

reviewed_declarations.name: AuditRound12.distinct_sectors_counterexample
reviewed_declarations.reason: Closed existential at n=1 only. Witness P=[[0,1],[1,0]] is symmetric and commutes with P. Its raw odd compression is -2 while the conjugated odd compression is +2; normalization gives -1 and +1. No Sturm-Liouville realization is asserted.

reviewed_declarations.name: AuditRound12.involutions
reviewed_declarations.reason: All n: P^2, E^2 and S^2 are identities on their own index types and all three matrices are symmetric. Swap squared is identity and each diagonal sign squares to 1.

reviewed_declarations.name: AuditRound12.normalization
reviewed_declarations.reason: Implicit n and arbitrary explicit K. The two Gram identities and two compressions use c^2=1/2 for c=(sqrt 2)^-1. Real sqrt(2) is nonzero without an extra theorem hypothesis. Valid at n=0.

reviewed_declarations.name: AuditRound12.odd_rank_one
reviewed_declarations.reason: Implicit n, every v : Fin n -> Real. With w=(v,-v), Bo^T w=2v and Be^T w=0, giving raw odd 4 vv^T, raw even zero, and conjugated odd zero. v!=0 is needed only for the last nonvanishing implication. A nonzero diagonal square proves nonvanishing, and at n=0 its premise is impossible. Normalized odd coefficient is 2.

intent_comparison: contract.md is explicitly real finite matrix algebra. Analytic Section 1 uses normalized columns and n>=1; the formal model uses raw columns with a proved normalization bridge and additionally covers n=0. Its generic compression identities have the same meaning. Complex coefficients, mixed-block identities and the equivalence with invariant-subspace decomposition are not formal target clauses.

For analytic Section 5, if Q=(q,q) in paired coordinates then S Q=(E q,-E q)=oddVector(E q). The formal odd outer-product theorem therefore supplies the relevant finite projection behavior conditional on that identification; it does not prove the Green expansions, spectral coefficients or spectral hypotheses.
